title: activity reports no agents when panes exist but none classify
description:
## Outcome

`ntm activity <session>` distinguishes "this session has no agent panes" from "there are panes
here and none of them could be classified". A session running six agents never reports that it
has none.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a session with live agent processes in its panes — including at least one pane whose
   tmux title is not an NTM-formatted agent name (an agent started outside `ntm spawn`, or one
   whose real process sits more than four levels below the pane's shell).
2. Run `ntm activity <session>`.
3. It prints `No agents found in session` while the panes and their processes are visibly there.

Observed on 2026-08-22 with six live agent processes in the session.

## Context

The message is emitted at `internal/cli/activity.go:591`, inside `renderActivityTUI`, guarded by
`if len(result.Agents) == 0`.

Discovery is **tmux pane inspection**, not a registry and not a process scan.
`collectActivityData` (`internal/cli/activity.go:252-311`) calls `tmux.GetPanes(session)`
(`internal/tmux/session.go:939`), classifies each pane through `detectAgentTypeFromPane`
(`internal/cli/activity.go:314`), and **skips any pane classified `unknown` or `user`**
(`internal/cli/activity.go:267-270`) — before `passesFilter` is ever consulted.

Classification itself is a three-step fallback at `internal/tmux/session.go:3087-3101`:
`parseAgentFromTitle(pane.Title)` looks for an NTM-formatted name such as `cc_1`, then
`pane.Command`, then `detectAgentFromProcessTree`, which walks **four** process levels.

So the empty list means: panes exist, and none of them parsed as a known agent from a title, a
command, or a shallow process walk. That is a **metadata-classification miss reported as an
absence** — the two states are indistinguishable in the output, and the one the operator sees is
the wrong one. An agent launched outside `ntm spawn` keeps its default shell title; an agent
nested more than four levels below the pane's shell defeats the tree walk.

The consequence is not cosmetic: the operator reads "no agents" and starts diagnosing the wrong
thing — whether the session died, whether the spawn worked — while the session is running
normally.

The narrow fix is to stop collapsing the two cases. Anything more — widening the process walk,
adding a fifth detection source — is a separate decision, because a deeper walk costs a `/proc`
traversal per pane on every refresh and this command is a TUI that refreshes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `tmux.GetPanes` returns zero panes, the output says the session has no panes
- [ ] When panes exist but every one classifies as `unknown` or `user`, the output says so and
      reports the count of unclassified panes — it never says "No agents found"
- [ ] The unclassified message names what to check: the pane title, the pane command, and that
      the process may sit deeper than the four levels
      `detectAgentFromProcessTree` walks (`internal/tmux/session.go:3092-3101`)
- [ ] Panes skipped as `user` are counted separately from panes skipped as `unknown` — one is
      expected, the other is a miss
- [ ] `--json` / robot output carries the same distinction as a field, so a caller can tell the
      two states apart without parsing prose
- [ ] The classification logic itself is unchanged: no new detection source and no deeper
      process walk in this bead
- [ ] The command's refresh cost is unchanged — no additional tmux or `/proc` call per pane
- [ ] Done when: a session with panes whose titles are plain shell titles reports "N panes, none
      classified as agents", and a session with no panes at all reports the empty-session
      message.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven in the convention of `internal/cli/activity_test.go` (plain
`func Test…` with case slices, e.g. `TestPassesFilter` at `:72`), over a stubbed pane list so no
tmux server is needed:

- zero panes → empty-session message
- panes present, all `unknown` → unclassified message with the correct count
- panes present, all `user` → its own message, counted separately
- a mix of `user`, `unknown` and one classified agent → the agent is rendered and the skipped
  counts are reported
- one classified agent only → today's output, unchanged (regression)
- the `--json` shape for each of the above → the state is a field, asserted by round-trip

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is a branch and a message.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/activity.go` — the skip at `267-270`, the empty guard and message at `591`, and
the result struct that carries the counts to the JSON path. `internal/tmux/session.go` is
**read, not modified**: `GetPanes` (`:939`) and the classification fallback (`3087-3101`) keep
their current behaviour, which is what makes this bead small and its regression risk local to
one command.

title: Surface a stale or failing bv instead of answering with nothing
description:
## Outcome

When the external `bv` binary is too old for the capabilities ntm asks of it, or fails outright,
`ntm work history` and `ntm work burndown` say so on stdout. Neither command can present a
degraded or empty answer as a real one, and the test suite can no longer pass while every real
`bv` failure mode goes unhandled.

## Steps to Reproduce

**A — `work history` reports zeros as data.** With `bv` v0.16.1 installed and a tracker whose
commit subjects all carry their bead ids, run `ntm work history`. It reports
`beads_with_commits: 0` over ~107 beads, every bead with `"commits":[]` and `"commit_index":{}`.
Nothing warns that the number is not a measurement.

**B — `work burndown` prints nothing.** Run `ntm work burndown current`. stdout receives zero
bytes. `bv --robot-burndown current` exits 1 and writes the plain text `No active sprint found`
to **stderr**, not JSON.

Both observed on 2026-08-22.

## Context

**Neither number is computed in this repo, and that is the key fact.**

`runWorkHistory` (`internal/cli/work.go:2734`) calls
`tools.NewBVAdapter().GetHistory` → `runRobotCommand(ctx, dir, "--robot-history")`
(`internal/tools/bv.go:226`, `:314`), which shells out to `bv` and passes its raw JSON through
unchanged in `--json` mode. ntm's own `HistoryStats` (`internal/cli/work.go:2663-2667`) carries
only `total_beads`, `total_commits` and `correlated_count` — **`beads_with_commits` is not an ntm
field at all**; it comes from `bv`, and the commit-subject matching that produces it lives inside
that binary.

`runWorkBurndown` (`internal/cli/work.go:3061`, command at `:2633` with `cobra.ExactArgs(1)`)
calls `adapter.GetBurndown` → `--robot-burndown <sprint>` (`internal/tools/bv.go:230`).
`runRobotCommand` (`internal/tools/bv.go:349-353`) turns any non-zero exit into a Go error, which
`runWorkBurndown` returns immediately — before any parsing or rendering. `cli.Execute()`
(`internal/cli/root.go:3155`, error path around `:3181-3202`) prints it as
`Error: …` on **stderr**. So there is no missing writer and no early return in ntm's render
path: `renderBurndown` (`internal/cli/work.go:3090`) always prints when it is reached, and it is
simply never reached. "Prints nothing" is what a stdout-only reader sees.

**The capability gate is the thing to distrust here, and it is wrong in the direction nobody
checked.** `internal/tools/bv.go:87-92` gates `robot_history` and `robot_burndown` behind
`bv >= 0.31`, and `robot_triage` / `robot_plan` / `robot_insights` / `robot_next` behind
`>= 0.30`. **No such `bv` has ever been published.** The tap that serves this machine reports
`dicklesworthstone/tap/bv: 0.16.1 -> stable 0.16.2` (read 2026-08-23), so every version the table
names is above everything that exists.

And the gated modes answer anyway on 0.16.1: `--robot-history` returned well-formed JSON, and
`--robot-burndown current` exited 1 with `No active sprint found` — a sprint lookup that ran, not
an unimplemented mode refusing. So the table reports as absent a capability the binary serves.

That inverts the obvious fix. A warning driven off the version comparison would fire on **every
run, for every user, forever**, and would call a working capability missing. The numbers in that
table are the first defect; the silence on real failure is the second. This bead fixes both, and
the reporting must key off observed behaviour rather than off the comparison.

**Why this shipped, and this is the part worth fixing hardest.** The contract test
(`internal/tools/contract_test.go:820-862`, table-driven `modeTest{name,key,call}`) runs against
a **fake `bv`** shell script at `testdata/faketools/bv`, injected by overriding `PATH`
(`internal/cli/work_test.go:195`). The fake always returns well-formed, non-empty JSON. It never
emulates a real `bv` that returns zero counts, that writes a plain-text error to stderr and
exits 1, or that reports a version below the capability gate. So the suite proves that a JSON
shape round-trips and nothing about how real `bv` behaviour is handled — a green test suite over
three live defects.

**The upstream half is explicitly out of scope.** `beads_with_commits` being zero while commit
subjects carry bead ids is a defect *inside* `bv`, in a repo this bead does not touch. The rule
here is the same one applied to `br`: a third-party tool gets an upstream issue or nothing.
What is in scope is that ntm must not present that number as though it measured it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The capability requirements at `internal/tools/bv.go:87-92` are corrected to versions that
      exist and that reflect what `bv` actually serves, verified by exercising each gated robot
      mode against the installed binary rather than by trusting the current numbers
- [ ] Degradation is reported from observed behaviour, never from the version comparison alone: a
      warning fires when a robot mode is unavailable or errors, and a `bv` that answers produces
      no warning at all
- [ ] When a warning does fire, `ntm work history` and `ntm work burndown` print it on **stdout**
      with the answer, naming the installed version and the capability that failed
- [ ] A non-zero exit from `bv` is surfaced on stdout, with `bv`'s own stderr text included, not
      only through the generic `Error:` path at `internal/cli/root.go:3181-3202`
- [ ] `ntm work burndown` with no active sprint prints a message a reader can act on and exits
      non-zero — zero bytes on stdout is never the answer
- [ ] `--json` output for both commands carries the degradation as a field (the `bv` version, the
      required version, whether the answer is complete), so an orchestrator can tell a real zero
      from an unavailable one
- [ ] `beads_with_commits` and its neighbours are passed through with their source named, so no
      reader takes an ntm-branded number for an ntm-computed one
- [ ] The fake `bv` at `testdata/faketools/bv` gains the real failure modes: a non-zero exit with
      plain-text stderr, a version below the gate, and a well-formed response with zero counts
- [ ] Each of those three fake behaviours is asserted by a test that **fails against today's
      code** — demonstrated by running it before the fix, not assumed
- [ ] A `bv` that serves every capability a command needs prints no warning — asserted, so the
      fix cannot degrade into an unconditional banner
- [ ] The existing contract cases keep passing unchanged
- [ ] Done when: with `bv` 0.16.1 installed, `ntm work history` prints its numbers with no
      spurious version warning, `ntm work burndown current` prints why it has nothing to show,
      and the only thing that warns is a capability the binary genuinely does not serve.

## Tests

**Unit tests** in the existing table-driven convention of
`internal/tools/contract_test.go:820-862`, driven by an extended fake `bv` under
`testdata/faketools/` selected by `PATH` (`internal/cli/work_test.go:195`):

- fake `bv` exits 1 with plain-text stderr → the text reaches stdout and the exit is non-zero
- fake `bv` reports a version below the gate but answers the robot mode → no warning (the case
  today's table gets wrong, and the one that would become a permanent banner)
- fake `bv` reports a version below the gate and refuses the robot mode → warning naming the
  installed version and the mode, and the command still answers what it can
- fake `bv` reports a version above the gate → no warning, output unchanged (regression)
- fake `bv` returns well-formed JSON with zero counts → the numbers are rendered with their
  source named
- fake `bv` returns malformed JSON → a message naming the tool, not a parse panic
- `work burndown` with no sprint argument → cobra's `ExactArgs(1)` message, unchanged

Plus one **end-to-end** case per command against the fake, asserting stdout is non-empty in every
failure mode — the single property that was missing.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is a subprocess boundary and its
messages.

## Recovery path

Nothing here migrates or writes state — both commands are read-only over `bv` and the tracker.
If the added warning proves too noisy, it is one revert of `internal/cli/work.go` and
`internal/tools/bv.go`; the capability table at `internal/tools/bv.go:88-107` is not being
changed, so no behaviour depends on the new code staying in place.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/work.go` (`runWorkHistory` at `2734`, `runWorkBurndown` at `3061`, `renderBurndown`
at `3090`), `internal/tools/bv.go` (`runRobotCommand` at `349-353` and the capability gate it
already carries at `88-107`), and the fake tool under `testdata/faketools/bv` plus the contract
tests. **No change to `bv` itself** — the zero-count defect is upstream and stays there; this
bead only stops ntm from repeating it silently.

title: Classify every robot query for session scope, and refuse an ignored --session
description:
## Outcome

Every registered `--robot-*` flag is classified in code as honouring `--session` or refusing it,
and a query in the refusing column that is handed `--session` returns `success:false` with a
machine-readable code and a hint, instead of accepting the flag and answering about a scope the
caller did not ask for. A robot query added later that is in neither column turns the test suite
red.

## Context

Split out of `bd-jlv68`, which scopes `--robot-snapshot` and settles the spelling: **the scope is
`--session`**, the shared root flag at `internal/cli/root.go:4787`, resolved through the
`resolveRobot…Session` helpers at `:5387-5401`. This bead is the sweep that applies that decision
to the whole surface.

**The inventory, measured 2026-08-23.** There are **154** registered `--robot-*` flags, declared
from `internal/cli/root.go:4118` through `:4691`. They are dispatched by the `Run:` closure of
`rootCmd` at `internal/cli/root.go:733-3144` — *not* by the if-chain at `:6346`, which is
`needsConfigLoading`, a config gate. They divide like this:

| bucket | count | what it is | column |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 4 | already resolve `--session` — `--robot-pipeline-run`, `--robot-tokens`, `--robot-alerts`, `--robot-palette` | honours |
| B | 50 | take the session as their own flag's value, e.g. `--robot-tail=proj` | refuses |
| C | 8 | per-session payload, ignore `--session` today | honours, after their own beads |
| D | 86 | no session dimension: tracker, config, doctor, accounts, quota, integrations | refuses |
| E | 6 | fleet aggregates | split by their own beads |

**The silent failure is measured, not hypothesised.** `--session` is registered on the same
`cobra.Command.Flags()` set as every robot flag, and cobra performs no cross-flag validation, so
it parses cleanly beside all 153 others and is then read in four dispatch branches only. Two
proofs from the code: `--robot-status` (`:763-772`) calls `robot.PrintStatusWithOptions`, whose
signature has no session argument, so `ntm --robot-status --session=foo` returns fleet-wide
status; and `ntm --robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2` (`:1631-1650`) reads `robotTail` and never
references `robotSharedSession`, so `proj2` is accepted and discarded without a word.

**Why bucket B refuses rather than converges.** Those 50 flags already carry their session as
their own value, and rewriting them into booleans plus `--session` would change half the robot
API's call syntax — every script, skill reference and doc that spells `--robot-tail=<session>`.
The repo owes no backwards compatibility (`AGENTS.md`, *Backwards Compatibility*), so that
rewrite is permitted, but it is a different and much larger piece of work than this sweep. Here,
`--session` alongside a bucket-B flag is refused, because a value that is accepted and discarded
is the exact defect this bead exists to end.

**Bucket C and E are settled elsewhere, and this bead depends on all of them**, because the
classification table can only be frozen once nothing is still moving between columns: the seven
bespoke session flags converge onto `--session` in their own bead, `--robot-rano-stats` gains a
filter in its own, `--robot-status` / `--robot-dashboard` / `--robot-terse` gain a scope in one
more, `--robot-snapshot` is `bd-jlv68`, and `--robot-inspect-coordination` /`--robot-restore` are
a `question` bead. This bead lands last and freezes the result.

**The error vocabulary does get one addition, and the earlier claim that it does not was wrong.**
None of the existing codes says what a refusal here means: `INVALID_FLAG`
(`internal/robot/types.go:92`) says the flag does not exist, but `--session` does exist and the
caller spelled it correctly — and reusing it makes `suggestNearestFlag`
(`internal/cli/root.go:456-486`) offer a "did you mean" for a flag that was typed right.
`SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (`:86`) says the session is missing, which is a different fact.
`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is exit code 2, documented in `AGENTS.md` as "skip gracefully" — the opposite
of what a caller should do here. So the refusal gets its own code.

Verified before this bead was written: **no wrapper in this repository passes `--session`
unconditionally to robot queries**, so turning acceptance into an error breaks no existing
caller. The single non-Go hit is `scripts/integration_master_test.sh:353`, which passes
`--session` to the `ntm history` subcommand, not to a robot flag.

Precedent for this class of defect in the same area: ntm#214, a deprecation hint pointing at a
flag that did not exist; its regression test is `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every one of the 154 registered `--robot-*` flags appears in exactly one column of a single
      classification table in code — honours `--session`, or refuses it — with no flag listed
      twice and none missing
- [ ] Passing `--session` to a flag in the refusing column returns `success:false`, exit code 1,
      and a new machine-readable `error_code` distinct from `INVALID_FLAG`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`
      and `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`
- [ ] That refusal carries a hint saying either which flag scopes this query (for the 50 that
      carry their session as their own value) or that the query has no session dimension (for the
      86 that do not)
- [ ] The new code is added to `internal/robot/types.go:86-92` alongside the existing constants
      and is documented in the error-code table in `AGENTS.md`
- [ ] `--robot-session` keeps returning `INVALID_FLAG` with the near-miss hint from
      `suggestNearestFlag` (`internal/cli/root.go:456-486`), and that hint names `--session`
- [ ] A test enumerates the registered `robot-*` flags from `rootCmd` at runtime and fails when a
      flag is in neither column — so a query added later cannot skip the decision
- [ ] Every query in the honouring column actually filters: for each, the scoped answer differs
      from the unscoped one when more than one session is live
- [ ] No robot query changes its output for a call that passes no `--session`
- [ ] The refusal path serialises a complete `RobotResponse` (`internal/robot/types.go:227-260`)
      with `success:false`, a non-empty `error_code` and no partial payload beside it
- [ ] Done when: `ntm --robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2` is refused instead of silently
      answering about `proj1`, and adding a robot flag without classifying it turns the suite red.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, in the style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go` (cobra
`ParseFlags` against a throwaway command), driven from the classification table so the whole list
is covered rather than a sample:

- `--session` on each refusing-column flag → refusal with the new code and a hint
- `--session` on each honouring-column flag → accepted, and the scoped answer differs from the
  unscoped one
- `--robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2` → refused, naming that `--robot-tail` carries its own
  session
- no `--session` passed → output unchanged from today, per query family (regression)
- `--robot-session` → `INVALID_FLAG` plus the near-miss hint naming `--session`
- the four bucket-A queries' resolution precedence → unchanged

**Unit test over the flag registry**: enumerate `rootCmd`'s `robot-…` flags at runtime, assert
each is in the table, and assert the table names no flag that is not registered — the case that
fails both when a query is added unclassified and when one is removed.

**Envelope round-trip test**, in the style of `internal/robot/envelope_test.go` and
`internal/robot/tui_parity_test.go:1177`: each refusal marshals and unmarshals to a complete
`RobotResponse`.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is flag parsing and JSON shape.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the robot flag declarations (`:4118-4691`), the dispatch closure
(`:733-3144`) where the refusal is applied in front of the handlers, the shared resolution
helpers (`:5387-5401`, `:4787`) and the error classification path (`:417-486`) — plus one new
classification table with its test, one new constant in `internal/robot/types.go:86-92`, and the
error-code table in `AGENTS.md`. **No robot query's payload computation is touched**: this bead
adds a guard in front of queries that ignore a flag and wires the ones that already scope into
the same table. Anything that gains a new filter is one of the beads this one depends on.

comments.author: da-review
comments.text: Measured 2026-08-24, evidence for the refusal column: 'ntm --robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2' reads proj1 and discards proj2 with no warning (internal/cli/root.go:1631-1650), and 'ntm --robot-status --session does-not-exist' answers success:true exit 0 with sessions:[]. Both are the accepted-and-ignored failure this bead ends. Note the exit-code convention the refusal must follow: a robot failure is carried in the JSON body and turned into a non-zero exit by encodeTerminalRobotOutput (internal/robot/robot.go:7742-7754) reaching recordRobotProcessExit (internal/cli/root.go:845-847); a nil Go error with success:false in the body is not enough on every handler, and --robot-status is one that exits 0 today.

title: Scope the fleet aggregates --robot-status, --robot-dashboard and --robot-terse to one session
description:
## Outcome

`--robot-status`, `--robot-dashboard` and `--robot-terse` accept `--session` and answer about
that session alone, resolving it the same way `--robot-snapshot` does. Unscoped, each behaves
exactly as it does today. The four fleet aggregates stop being the only state surfaces an
orchestrator cannot narrow.

## Context

These three are fleet aggregates: they walk every session and every pane and answer about all of
them, with no filter of any kind.

- `--robot-status` (`internal/cli/root.go:763-772`) calls
  `robot.PrintStatusWithOptions(pagination)` — the call takes no session argument at all
- `--robot-dashboard` (`:1013-1014`) calls `robot.PrintDashboard(jsonOutput)`
- `--robot-terse` (`:2544-2545`) calls `robot.PrintTerse(cfg)`

`--session` is registered on the same flag set (`internal/cli/root.go:4787`) as every other robot
flag, so cobra parses it here without complaint and the value is then never read. Measured
2026-08-23: `ntm --robot-status --session=foo` returns fleet-wide status, silently. That is the
defect this bead removes for three of the four aggregates; the fourth, `--robot-snapshot`, is
`bd-jlv68`, which establishes the convention this bead follows rather than reinventing.

They are one bead because they are one shape: three read-only aggregations over the same session
and pane inventory, differing in rendering. Splitting them would triple the cost of a change that
is a filter applied at the same place three times.

The resolution path to reuse is the one the four bucket-A queries already use —
`resolveRobot…Session` (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`) falling back to `robotSharedSession`
(`:4787`), with precedence covered by `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`.

The remaining two ambiguous flags are **not** in this bead. `--robot-inspect-coordination`
(`:2679`) is keyed by agent name, and NATO-phonetic agent names repeat across sessions;
`--robot-restore` (`:2598`) is keyed by a save-file path that may itself name a session. Both are
decisions rather than filters, and they carry their own `question` bead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of `--robot-status`, `--robot-dashboard` and `--robot-terse` accepts `--session` and
      returns only that session's sessions/panes/agents data
- [ ] Each resolves the session through the shared helper path (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`),
      not through three separate resolutions written per query
- [ ] Called with no `--session`, each produces output byte-identical to today's — asserted, not
      assumed
- [ ] A `--session` naming a session that does not exist returns `success:false` with
      `error_code: SESSION_NOT_FOUND` for all three, never an empty success
- [ ] The scoped answer of each differs from its unscoped answer whenever more than one session
      is live — the criterion that proves the filter is applied rather than accepted
- [ ] Pagination on `--robot-status` (`robot.PrintStatusWithOptions`) keeps working under a
      scope: limits and offsets apply to the filtered set, not to the fleet
- [ ] The four bucket-A queries and `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49` are untouched
- [ ] Done when: with two live sessions, `ntm --robot-status --session <one>` names only that
      session's panes, and `ntm --robot-status` still names both.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, over a stubbed session and pane inventory so no tmux server is
needed, in the style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go`:

- each query scoped to one of two stub sessions → only that session's entries
- each query unscoped → both sessions, output unchanged from today (regression)
- unknown session name → `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` for each
- `--robot-status` scoped with pagination → the page is taken from the filtered set

**Envelope round-trip test**, in the style of `internal/robot/envelope_test.go`: the scoped and
the failing responses each serialise a complete `RobotResponse`, with no partial payload
alongside an error.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is a filter and a flag.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the three dispatch branches at `:763-772`, `:1013-1014` and
`:2544-2545`, plus the shared resolution helpers at `:5387-5401` — and the signatures of
`robot.PrintStatusWithOptions`, `robot.PrintDashboard` and `robot.PrintTerse` in
`internal/robot/`, each of which gains an optional session scope. No other robot query is
touched, no pattern or classifier is involved, and nothing outside these three renderings changes
shape.

comments.author: da-review
comments.text: Measured 2026-08-24 against the binary built from agent/bd-jlv68: 'ntm --robot-status --session does-not-exist' returns success:true, exit 0, with sessions:[] — it accepts an unknown session scope and answers as though it had filtered. The scoped --robot-snapshot landed by bd-jlv68 is strictly stricter: same input returns success:false, error_code SESSION_NOT_FOUND, exit 1. So scoping --robot-status here must also make an unknown session an error, not an empty success; the two aggregates disagreeing is how the silent-wrong-scope defect survives in a second shape.

title: Deliver spawn prompts to pi panes: readiness resolves state=unknown at 0.25
description:
## Outcome

`ntm spawn` delivers prompts to `pi` panes. A six-pane pi swarm launches with every prompt
delivered, instead of every pane failing `user_prompt readiness ... timeout ... last
state=unknown freshness=fresh confidence=0.25` while sitting at a healthy pi prompt. The
readiness poll — not only the classifier layer under it — is covered by a test for a
non-`cc`/`cod` agent type, so the next classifier that lands is known to reach the gate that
uses it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install ntm at `d58a18eb` or later (`bin/binary-drift` clean; `ntm --version` reports
   `v1.26.0-16-gd58a18eb`). This is the commit that merged PR #3 and therefore already
   carries `0a771c3a`, "give pi a readiness classifier".
2. `ntm spawn` a six-pane session with agent type `pi`.
3. Every pane comes up at a working pi prompt.
4. Spawn fails all six:

```
spawn prompt setup failed: pane %252: agent 1 (pi): user_prompt readiness for pane %252:
timeout waiting for pane %252 to become ready; last state=unknown freshness=fresh
confidence=0.25; pane %253: agent 2 (pi): ... (and so on for all six)
```

No prompt is delivered to any pane. Recovery is manual delivery to six panes.

Observed three times on that binary, on separate days: 2026-08-22 15:20, 2026-08-23 17:57 and
2026-08-23 21:20, six panes each, 18 of 18 panes, identical signature every time. Recorded in
the kernl-da run ledger (`~/.local/state/kernl-da/runs.jsonl`, `bin/run-log friction`), where
`ntm` is the largest non-`Bash` friction bucket of the window — 17 rows across 13 of 33 runs,
10 of them readiness or delivery.

## Context

**This is not the stale-binary case, and it is not the case bd-zz717 covers.** Two nearby
explanations are already ruled out:

- The 2026-08-22 12:15 session replaced the installed binary (its backup is named
  `ntm.pre-pi-readiness-v1.24.0-3-g28bd96c9`), so the three reproductions above ran on the
  commit that added pi classification, not before it.
- `bd-zz717` makes the readiness verdict *visible* per pane at spawn. Visibility is worth
  having and would have shortened the diagnosis, but a verdict line does not deliver a prompt.
  This bead is the delivery failing; that one is nobody being told.

**Where the failure sits, traced but not closed.** The timeout string is built by
`spawnReadinessError` off `waitForSpawnPaneReady` (`internal/cli/spawn.go`), which polls every
`spawnReadyPollInterval` (200ms) until `spawnPromptReadyTimeout` (30s). Readiness needs
`spawnPaneObservationSafeToDispatch`, which requires both `pane.SafeToDispatch()` and an
independent re-parse through `agent.NewParser().ParseWithHint`. `SafeToDispatch`
(`internal/status/types.go`) demands `State == StateIdle` and `Confidence >=
minimumDispatchConfidence` (0.75). The observed `0.25` is pinned by `observationConfidence`
(`internal/status/unified.go`) for any `StateUnknown`, so an unknown state can never pass.

`0a771c3a` added pi to exactly the registries that chain reads — `internal/agent/{parser,
patterns,types}.go` and `internal/status/{patterns,unified}.go`, including a pi arm in
`determineStateAt`. So the classifier is reachable from the poll, and the panes still resolve
to `unknown`. `composerMarkerForAgent` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2203`, entries for
`AgentClaude` and `AgentCodex` only) is a different table and is not the cause: it fails open
for unlisted types and gates a keystroke preflight and a reporting-only verdict, never this
timeout.

**The one path not yet traced, and the first place to look:** how a pane's `Pane.Type` is
derived from its tmux title and fed to `buildPaneObservation`'s `normalizedAgentType`. If a pi
pane's type does not normalise to `AgentTypePi` at that point, `determineStateAt` never enters
the pi arm at all and falls through to the generic path — which produces exactly
`StateUnknown` at 0.25 on a pane whose text is a perfectly good pi prompt. That is consistent
with every field in the observed error, `freshness=fresh` included: the capture is current,
it is the classification that is empty.

**Why the existing test suite did not catch it.** `TestDetermineStatePiPaneIsNotUnknown`
(added by `0a771c3a`) proves the classifier layer resolves a pi capture, and it passes. Nothing
exercises `waitForSpawnPaneReady` or `spawnPaneObservationSafeToDispatch` *succeeding* for any
type outside `cc`/`cod`. `TestDispatchSpawnPromptSequenceReadinessTimeout` covers the timeout
path for `AgentClaude` only. So the layer under the gate is tested green while the gate itself
is untested for the type that fails — which is why a merged, correct-looking classifier fix
changed nothing in production.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A six-pane `pi` spawn delivers all six prompts: `ntm spawn` exits 0 with no
      `spawn prompt setup failed` line, and each pane's scrollback shows its prompt text.
- [ ] The readiness poll observes a live pi pane as `state=idle` with `confidence >= 0.75`
      within the 30s `spawnPromptReadyTimeout` — verified from the observation, not from the
      absence of an error.
- [ ] `Pane.Type` normalises a pi pane to `AgentTypePi` at `buildPaneObservation`, or the
      report says why the type is something else and the fix is made where it belongs.
- [ ] The three reproductions above re-run on the fixed binary produce zero readiness
      timeouts across 18 panes.
- [ ] Done when: a six-pane pi swarm can be launched twice in a row with no manual prompt
      delivery.

## Tests

- **Unit** — `spawnPaneObservationSafeToDispatch` returns true for a pi observation built from
  a real captured pi prompt, and false for a pi pane mid-work. This is the assertion the suite
  is missing today; it must fail against the current binary before the fix.
- **Unit** — `normalizedAgentType` / `Pane.Type` derivation maps a tmux pane titled as ntm
  titles a pi pane to `AgentTypePi`. Table-driven over every type in `knownAgentTypes`, so the
  next agent type added cannot repeat this silently.
- **Integration** — `waitForSpawnPaneReady` against a fake observer that yields a pi
  observation, asserting it returns before the deadline. The existing timeout test covers only
  `AgentClaude` and only the failing direction.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/spawn.go` (the poll and its gate), `internal/status/unified.go` (state and
confidence), and whichever file in `internal/tmux` derives `Pane.Type` from the pane title —
the third is the one the trace has not pinned yet, and finding it is part of the work. Their
tests: `internal/cli/spawn_state_test.go` and `internal/status/unified_test.go`. No schema, no
robot-API surface, no change to the delivery mechanism itself.

## Recovery path

None needed — no state is migrated and no data is rewritten. If a fix regresses the
`cc`/`cod` path, revert the commit; readiness is computed per spawn and nothing persists
between runs.

title: Dispatch gate withholds work from a pane whose scrollback holds a stale error
description:
## Outcome

The coordinator's dispatch gate stops withholding work from a pane whose only sign of trouble is
an error string left in its scrollback. The gate reads a verdict that carries the live-tail and
progress guard, so the fix landed in `bd-j5cdo` reaches the surface that acts on it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an agent pane of a type with no actively-working short-circuit in the static detector —
   gemini, cursor, windsurf, aider, ollama, or a pane classified `unknown`.
2. Let it emit a transient error line, then let it recover and keep producing output.
3. Ask the coordinator for assignment candidates while the pane is working.
4. The pane is skipped: it is not offered work for as long as the offending line stays inside the
   static scan window.

Measured 2026-08-23, after `bd-j5cdo` landed the live-tail plus progress guard on the robot
classifier.

## Context

`bd-j5cdo` fixed the robot classifier: an error pattern matching outside the live tail no longer
produces `error` while the pane is demonstrably progressing. Verified there by breaking each
guard and watching the tests go red.

**The coordinator does not read that classifier for its status.** `resultFromPaneObservation`
(`internal/coordinator/monitor.go:182`) sets `Status: mapStatusToRobotState(current.Status.State)`
— the verdict of the *static* detector in `internal/status`. Lines `195-202` do call the robot
classifier, but assign only `result.Velocity`; there is no `Status` override. Compare
`GetAgentStatus` (`monitor.go:110-114`) and `GetAgentStatusWithOutput` (`:151-155`), which both
carry `if activity.State == robot.StateError { … }` and do override.

That path is the live one: `SessionCoordinator.updateAgentStatesContext`
(`internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:628`) calls it. `GetAllAgentStatuses` and
`GetAgentStatusWithOutput` have no callers in the tree at all, so fixing them would fix nothing.

**What acts on it, and what does not** — established by reading the consumers rather than
assuming:

- **Dispatch gating — yes.** `getAssignmentCandidates` (`internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:403`)
  skips any agent whose `Status` is `robot.StateError`. A working pane is withheld from
  assignment.
- **The `agent.error` event — yes** (`coordinator.go:775`), reaching webhooks, `internal/notify`
  and the attention feed (`internal/robot/attention_feed.go:3140`, `ActionRequired`,
  `SeverityError`). A false alarm rather than a destructive act.
- **The digest** — display only (`internal/coordinator/digest.go:109`).
- **Restart — no.** The resilience restart path runs on `internal/health` plus PID liveness;
  `internal/health` does not import `robot` and holds no `StateError` reference. The static
  verdict never reaches a restart decision, which bounds how much this costs.

**The obvious fix is the wrong one, and this is the part worth reading before starting.** Adding
the same override `GetAgentStatus` carries would change nothing here: that override is one-way —
it escalates to `StateError`, it never clears one. The defect is a *false* error coming out of the
static detector, so what is needed is the robot verdict being able to **downgrade** a static
`StateError`, which is a different change from the symmetry argument it looks like.

**Which panes are exposed.** In `internal/status/unified.go`, `DetectErrorInOutput` (~`:204`) runs
before the `StateWorking` branch (~`:218`). Claude, Codex and pi have earlier actively-working
short-circuits (~`:129`, `:145`, `:174`), and an idle pane at a prompt is rescued at `:186`. Every
other type is exposed. The window is bounded: the static scan is the last 50 lines
(`internal/status/errors.go:96`), so what is exposed is the band between the robot classifier's
width-adaptive live tail and that 50-line bound — narrow, and not empty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A progressing pane of an exposed type (gemini, cursor, windsurf, aider, ollama, unknown)
      with a stale error outside the live tail is offered work by `getAssignmentCandidates`
      (`internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:403`)
- [ ] The same pane with a *current* error in the live tail is still withheld, and still emits
      `agent.error` (`coordinator.go:775`)
- [ ] A pane that is genuinely stuck — a stale error and no output growth between captures — is
      still withheld: the fix must not turn the gate off, only stop it firing on recovered panes
- [ ] `resultFromPaneObservation` (`internal/coordinator/monitor.go:182`) reaches its `Status`
      through a verdict that carries the live-tail and progress guard, and the code says which
      classifier decides
- [ ] The robot verdict can DOWNGRADE a static `StateError`, not only escalate to one — asserted
      by a test, because the one-way override is the trap this bead exists to avoid
- [ ] Claude, Codex and pi panes classify exactly as they do today — their short-circuits already
      rescue them, so their behaviour is a regression surface, not a target
- [ ] No additional tmux capture per coordinator tick: the robot classifier is already called on
      this path for `Velocity`, so the verdict costs no new I/O
- [ ] The comment at `internal/status/unified.go:190-203` is updated to match whatever this bead
      makes true
- [ ] Done when: a fixture pane of an exposed type, progressing with `invalid_api_key` five lines
      back, appears in the assignment candidates, and the same pane with the match in its live
      tail does not.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, over stubbed pane observations so no tmux server is needed, in the
convention of `internal/robot/activity_test.go` and the coordinator's own tests:

- exposed type, stale error, progressing → candidate, no `agent.error`
- exposed type, live-tail error → withheld, `agent.error` emitted
- exposed type, stale error, no growth → withheld (the stuck pane)
- claude / codex / pi, each shape → unchanged from today (regression)
- the downgrade path directly: a static `StateError` plus a robot verdict of working → the result
  is working, asserted at the function that decides it

**Regression test** that `getAssignmentCandidates` still skips a genuinely errored agent, so the
gate is not quietly disabled by this change.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is a classification hand-off between two
existing components.

## Blast radius

`internal/coordinator/monitor.go` — `resultFromPaneObservation` (`:182`) and its use of the robot
classifier at `:195-202` — and the comment at `internal/status/unified.go:190-203`. The static
detector's own logic, the robot classifier landed by `bd-j5cdo`, the error pattern tables and the
restart machinery are **read, not changed**. `getAssignmentCandidates` (`coordinator.go:403`) and
the `agent.error` emission (`:775`) keep their current conditions; what changes is the verdict
they are handed.

title: A stale error string in the scrollback classifies a working pane as error
description:
## Outcome

A pane that is actively producing output is not classified `error` because of a string left in
its scrollback minutes ago. An error match only wins while it is the pane's *current* state, so
the surfaces that act on `error` — dispatch gating, health restarts, `ntm wait` — stop acting on
a pane that is working.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn an agent pane and let it produce a transient error line — an expired-credential
   message, or a Go binary printing `Error: context canceled` from a bare `ctx.Err()`.
2. Let the agent recover and keep working: the pane is generating output and spending tokens.
3. Read the pane's state through any robot/coordinator surface.
4. The pane reports `state:error` while it is demonstrably working, and keeps reporting it for
   as long as the offending line stays inside the capture window.

Observed on 2026-08-22 with `ctx.Err()` and `invalid_api_key` in the scrollback of healthy,
token-spending panes.

## Context

There are **two independent classifiers**, both driven purely by captured pane *text* — neither
reads a process or exit-status signal:

- `determineStateAt`, `internal/status/unified.go:106`, producing `status.AgentState`
  (`idle`/`working`/`error`/`unknown`, `internal/status/types.go:14-23`).
- `StateClassifier.Classify`, `internal/robot/activity.go:892`, producing `robot.AgentState`
  (`internal/robot/patterns.go:24-25`), used by the coordinator, health and dispatch surfaces.

Each carries its own error table: `errorPatterns` at `internal/status/errors.go:29-84` — the
credential regex at `:45` matches `invalid_api_key`, and a generic `(?im)^error:` prefix at
`:88` catches any line starting `Error:`, including `Error: context canceled` — and a parallel
table at `internal/robot/patterns.go:155` (`invalid_key`) and `:167` (`api_error`).

**The defect is not the patterns. It is where they are allowed to match, and what a match
outranks.**

- `classifyInternal` (`internal/robot/activity.go:928`) runs the pattern match over the **full**
  captured buffer — `LinesStatusDetection = 20` lines
  (`internal/tmux/capture_helpers.go:26`) — separately from the smaller live tail it computes at
  `internal/robot/activity.go:945`.
- `classifyState` (`internal/robot/activity.go:1218-1220`) gives `CategoryError` **absolute
  priority** at confidence 0.95.
- `applyHysteresis` (`internal/robot/activity.go:1279-1290`) lets `StateError` transition
  **immediately**, with no debounce — every other transition is damped.
- The one guard against a stale match, `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle`
  (`internal/robot/activity.go:1162`), strips the stale error from the full buffer **only when
  the live tail currently shows a fresh idle prompt** (`hasLiveIdle`, `:1176-1181`). When the
  pane is *not* idle — that is, precisely when it is working — the guard no-ops and returns the
  full buffer unchanged (`:1181-1182`).

So the guard covers the harmless case and misses the harmful one. A pane that has gone quiet is
protected; a pane that is busy is not.

The scan scope is bounded in both classifiers and is not the problem to fix: the robot path
captures 20 lines, and `status.DetectErrorInOutput` re-scans the last 50
(`internal/status/errors.go:97-99`, `ScanLines = 50` from `DefaultConfig()`,
`internal/status/detector.go:23`).

**Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug: the consumers act, and one of them is
destructive.**

- `internal/coordinator/monitor.go:110-114` and `:151-155` — overrides the static detector and
  clears `SafeToDispatch`, so a working pane stops receiving work.
- `internal/robot/health.go:604-605` — `checkErrors` / stall detection feeding `RestartManager`
  (`internal/robot/health.go:1646-1750`).
- `internal/robot/diagnose.go:650` — the `ntm diagnose --restart` path.
- `internal/cli/wait.go:239-242` — `ntm wait` fails with `WaitErrorStateError`.
- `internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:775` — emits an `agent.error` event.

A restart of a pane that was merely displaying old text discards whatever that agent had in
context. That is the failure mode this bead exists to remove, and it is the reason the fix must
not simply lengthen the debounce.

An operator-side note that should not be mistaken for the fix: readers already know a pane's
`error` is sniffed from visible text and has to be corroborated before acting. This bead removes
the need for that corroboration in the common case; it does not make `error` a certainty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An error pattern matching **outside** the live tail does not by itself produce `error`
      while the pane shows evidence of progress (output growth between two captures)
- [ ] The same pattern matching **inside** the live tail still produces `error` immediately, with
      today's confidence and today's lack of debounce
- [ ] `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle` (`internal/robot/activity.go:1162`) — or its replacement —
      covers the working case as well as the idle one, and its name and comment say which cases
      it covers
- [ ] The static classifier at `internal/status/unified.go:106` reaches the same verdict as the
      robot classifier for identical input, or the divergence is documented in a comment naming
      why two answers are correct
- [ ] No consumer changes behaviour for a pane that is genuinely in error: dispatch gating,
      health restart, `ntm diagnose --restart`, `ntm wait` and the `agent.error` event all still
      fire on a real error
- [ ] Classification cost does not grow: no additional tmux capture per classification, and the
      scan window stays at 20 lines for the robot path and 50 for the static one
- [ ] Done when: a fixture pane whose buffer contains `invalid_api_key` five lines back and
      whose tail is actively growing classifies as working, and the same buffer with the match
      in the tail classifies as error.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven with fixture scrollback strings, in the convention of
`internal/status/errors_test.go` (`TestDetectErrorInOutput_*`), `internal/status/unified_test.go`
and `internal/robot/patterns.go`'s own test neighbours. One case per row:

- error string in the live tail, pane idle → `error`
- error string in the live tail, pane working → `error`
- error string outside the live tail, pane idle → not `error` (today's guard, must not regress)
- error string outside the live tail, pane working → **not** `error` (the defect)
- `Error: context canceled` outside the tail, pane working → not `error`
- no error string anywhere → unchanged
- two consecutive captures with no growth and a stale error → `error` (a genuinely stuck pane is
  still caught)

Plus a **regression test asserting hysteresis is unchanged** for every non-error transition
(`internal/robot/activity.go:1279-1290`), so a fix to the error path does not quietly damp the
others.

## Blast radius

`internal/robot/activity.go` — `classifyInternal` (928), `classifyState` (1218-1220),
`applyHysteresis` (1279-1290) and `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle` (1162-1182) — and, if the two
classifiers are reconciled, `internal/status/unified.go:106`. The error pattern tables
(`internal/status/errors.go:29-88`, `internal/robot/patterns.go:155-167`) are **not** edited:
the strings are right, the placement rule is wrong. No consumer is modified; every one of the
five listed above keeps its current behaviour on a real error.

title: Converge the bespoke per-query session flags onto --session
description:
## Outcome

The six robot queries that scope by a session flag of their own read the shared `--session` flag
instead, and their bespoke flag names are gone. `--robot-mail` resolves its session the same way.
After this bead there is exactly one spelling of "which session" for every query that filters by
one, and no caller has to remember which query invented which name.

## Context

An inventory of the whole robot surface on 2026-08-23 counted **154** registered `--robot-*`
flags. They divide by session scope like this:

| bucket | count | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 4 | already read the shared `--session` (`internal/cli/root.go:4787`) |
| B | 50 | take the session as their own flag's value (`--robot-tail=proj`) |
| C | 8 | answer about per-session state and ignore `--session` |
| D | 86 | no session dimension at all |
| E | 6 | fleet aggregates, ambiguous |

This bead is bucket C minus one. Seven of the eight already filter by session — they just do it
under a name each query invented for itself:

- `--events-session` for `--robot-events` (`internal/cli/root.go:832`)
- `--attention-session` for `--robot-attention` (`:883`) and, reused, `--robot-digest` (`:917`)
- `--overlay-session` for `--robot-overlay` (`:1112`)
- `--md-session` for `--robot-markdown` (`:2550`)
- `--dismiss-session` for `--robot-dismiss-alert` (`:2824`)
- `--robot-mail` (`:1173`) takes no session flag at all: it reads a positional argument, or infers
  the session from the working directory or the surrounding tmux client

The eighth, `--robot-rano-stats`, has no session filtering of any kind and is its own bead.

Five names for one concept is the tech debt the repo's own `AGENTS.md` refuses ("Never create
compatibility shims… Just fix the code directly", and no backwards compatibility is owed because
the project has no external users). So the bespoke flags are **deleted**, not aliased: an alias
would leave six spellings instead of five and would be exactly the shim that file forbids.

The resolution machinery to converge onto already exists and is proven: the four bucket-A queries
resolve through `resolveRobotPipelineSession` / `resolveRobotTokensSession` /
`resolveRobotAlertsSession` / `resolveRobotPaletteSession` (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`),
each falling back to `robotSharedSession` bound at `:4787`. Its precedence is covered by
`internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`.

`--robot-mail` is the one that needs a judgement rather than a rename: its cwd and tmux inference
is a convenience worth keeping, so `--session` becomes the highest-precedence source and the
inference remains the fallback when no flag is given.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--robot-events`, `--robot-attention`, `--robot-digest`, `--robot-overlay`,
      `--robot-markdown` and `--robot-dismiss-alert` all resolve their session from `--session`
      through the same helper path as the four bucket-A queries (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`)
- [ ] `--events-session`, `--attention-session`, `--overlay-session`, `--md-session` and
      `--dismiss-session` no longer exist: passing one returns `INVALID_FLAG` through
      `classifyRobotExecuteError` (`internal/cli/root.go:417-448`), and the near-miss hint from
      `suggestNearestFlag` (`:456-486`) names `--session`
- [ ] No alias, no deprecation shim and no hidden flag is left behind for the five removed names
- [ ] `--robot-mail` reads `--session` when it is given, and keeps its positional-argument, cwd
      and tmux inference unchanged as the fallback when it is not — precedence asserted in that
      order
- [ ] Every one of the six queries returns the same payload for a given session as it does today
      when that session is passed the new way — the change is the flag, never the answer
- [ ] A session named through `--session` that does not exist returns `success:false` with
      `error_code: SESSION_NOT_FOUND` for all six, matching the bucket-A behaviour
- [ ] The four bucket-A queries and their precedence test
      (`internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`) are untouched and still pass
- [ ] Every reference to a removed flag name in the repository's own docs is updated in the same
      commit — `grep` for each of the five names comes back empty outside the changelog
- [ ] Done when: `ntm --robot-events --session <name>` answers for that session, and
      `ntm --robot-events --events-session <name>` returns `INVALID_FLAG` with a hint naming
      `--session`.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, in the style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go` (cobra
`ParseFlags` against a throwaway command):

- each of the six queries with `--session` → resolves to that session
- each of the five removed flag names → `INVALID_FLAG` plus a hint naming `--session`
- `--robot-mail` with `--session` → the flag wins over the positional argument and over the cwd
  inference
- `--robot-mail` with no `--session` → today's inference, unchanged (regression)
- an unknown session on each of the six → `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`

**Unit test over the flag registry**: enumerate `rootCmd`'s registered flags and assert none of
the five removed names is present — the case that fails if one is quietly restored as an alias.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is flag parsing and resolution
precedence.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the six dispatch branches named above, the flag declarations for the
five removed names, and the shared resolution helpers at `:5387-5401`. The payload functions in
`internal/robot/` are called with a session the same way they are today, so no query's output
computation is touched. `--robot-rano-stats` and the 50 bucket-B queries are out of scope, as is
the refusal rule for queries with no session dimension.

title: Scope --robot-snapshot to one session with the existing --session flag
description:
## Outcome

A robot caller can scope `--robot-snapshot` to one session, spelled with the `--session` flag
that already exists, and a scope naming a session that is not there is refused with
`SESSION_NOT_FOUND` instead of answered with an empty success. The reported
`{"name":null,"panes":[]}` observation is settled — reproduced and fixed, or refuted and
recorded.

## Context

Two symptoms were reported from one session on 2026-08-22: `--robot-snapshot` has no way to
filter by session, and a near-miss flag failed **two different ways** — once with `INVALID_FLAG`,
once returning `{"name":null,"panes":[]}` with no error at all.

What the code says:

- There are roughly **140** `--robot-*` flags, declared as one block of
  `rootCmd.Flags().BoolVar/StringVar` calls beginning at `internal/cli/root.go:4118`. They all
  belong to a single flat command — cobra dispatches on which flag was set, through an `if`
  chain (`internal/cli/root.go:6346`).
- **`--robot-session` does not exist.** An exhaustive scan of every registered `"robot-…"`
  literal in `root.go` has no such flag. So `INVALID_FLAG` is the *correct* answer for it, and
  the near-miss machinery already helps: `classifyRobotExecuteError`
  (`internal/cli/root.go:417-448`) maps cobra parse errors to codes and `suggestNearestFlag`
  (`:456-486`) adds a Levenshtein "did you mean" hint.
- Session scoping exists, but unevenly. A shared root flag `--session`
  (`internal/cli/root.go:4787`) feeds **only four** robot queries —
  `--robot-pipeline-run`, `--robot-tokens`, `--robot-alerts`, `--robot-palette` — through their
  `resolveRobot…Session` helpers (`internal/cli/root.go:3396+`). Separately,
  `--robot-inspect-session=<name>` (`internal/cli/root.go:4548`) takes the name as its own
  value. Everything else ignores `--session` entirely.
- `--robot-snapshot` (`internal/cli/root.go:4128`) is documented as "Unified state: sessions +
  beads + alerts + mail" and covers **all** sessions. Its only filter is `--since`
  (`internal/cli/root.go:805-820`), which is delta pagination, not scope. This confirms the
  reported gap directly.

**The second symptom is the more interesting one and it is not yet confirmed.** A flag that does
not exist cannot produce a silent empty answer — pflag rejects it before any handler runs. No
producer of a literal `"name":null` alongside a `panes` array was found in the tree; the two
structurally closest types are `SessionInfo` (`internal/robot/robot.go:1563`) and
`InspectSessionOutput` / `InspectSessionDetail` (`internal/cli/tui_parity.go:339-365`), and
neither naturally serialises `name` as JSON `null`. The most likely explanation is that the call
passed the **valid** `--session` flag to a robot query that never reads it: parsing succeeds,
the filter is a no-op, and the answer describes an unintended scope. That is a hypothesis, not a
finding, and settling it is part of this bead rather than an assumption inside it.

There is precedent for exactly this class of defect in the session-flag area: ntm#214, where a
deprecation hint pointed at a flag that did not exist — the regression test for it is
`internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`.

**Two decisions were taken before this bead was dispatched, and neither is open.**

1. **The scope is spelled `--session`** — the shared root flag at `internal/cli/root.go:4787`,
   reused. No new session flag is introduced, and `--robot-snapshot` joins the four queries that
   already resolve it through their `resolveRobot…Session` helpers (`:3396+`) rather than taking
   a name of its own the way `--robot-inspect-session` does. The precedent, the resolution
   helpers and the regression test all exist; a second spelling would be a second thing to keep
   true.
2. **The uniform refusal rule is not in this bead.** Classifying ~135 robot queries into
   honours-a-scope and does-not, and refusing `--session` on the second column, is a sweep over
   the whole robot surface rather than a change to one handler. It is `bd-5u429`, which depends
   on this bead because its hint text names the flag this bead makes work.

The envelope needed for a clean refusal already exists: `RobotResponse`
(`internal/robot/types.go:227-260`) carries `success`, `error`, `error_code` and `hint`, with
constants including `INVALID_FLAG` (`internal/robot/types.go:92`) and `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`
(`:86`). So this bead adds no new error vocabulary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--robot-snapshot` accepts a session scope, and the scoped answer contains only that
      session's data while the unscoped call behaves exactly as it does today
- [ ] A session scope naming a session that does not exist returns `success:false` with
      `error_code: SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, not an empty success
- [ ] `--robot-snapshot` resolves `--session` through the same helper path as the four queries
      that already do (`internal/cli/root.go:3396+`), not through a second resolution written for
      this one query
- [ ] `--robot-session` keeps returning `INVALID_FLAG` with the near-miss hint, and the hint now
      names the flag that actually scopes the query the caller was reaching for
- [ ] The `{"name":null,"panes":[]}` observation is reproduced or refuted, and the finding is
      recorded on this bead — if it is a real code path, it is fixed here; if it was `--session`
      passed to a query that ignores it, that is recorded and left to `bd-5u429`
- [ ] The four queries that resolve `--session` today
      (`internal/cli/root.go:3396+`) keep their current resolution precedence, asserted by the
      existing test
- [ ] Done when: `--robot-snapshot --session <name>` returns that session and no other, an
      unknown name returns `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, and the unscoped call is byte-identical to
      today's.

## Tests

**Unit tests** in the two conventions already present:

- flag parsing and resolution, in the style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go`
  (table-style, cobra `ParseFlags` against a throwaway command): scoped snapshot accepted and
  filtered; unknown session → `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; unscoped snapshot unchanged;
  `--robot-session` → `INVALID_FLAG` plus the near-miss suggestion; the four existing queries'
  precedence unchanged.
- envelope shape, in the style of `internal/robot/envelope_test.go` and
  `internal/robot/tui_parity_test.go:1177` (marshal/unmarshal round-trips rather than golden
  files): every new failure path serialises a complete `RobotResponse` with `success:false`, a
  non-empty `error_code`, and no partial payload alongside it.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is flag parsing and JSON shape. The
inventory test over every robot flag belongs to `bd-5u429`, not here.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the `--robot-snapshot` handler and its flag declaration (`:4118-4128`),
the `--session` resolution helpers (`:3396+`, `:4787`), and the error classification path
(`:417-486`) — plus the robot output type behind snapshot in `internal/robot/`. The error
constants in `internal/robot/types.go:86-92` are reused, not extended. The four queries that
already resolve `--session`, and `--robot-inspect-session`, keep their behaviour; the other ~135
robot flags are not touched by this bead at all — the rule that applies uniformly to them is
`bd-5u429`.
